column1: # The label taxonomy, one definition for every repo on every board.
# Columns: group <TAB> name <TAB> colour <TAB> description
# Every issue carries at least one TYPE label and one AREA label. A type says what
# sort of work it is; an area says which part of the product it touches. A closes
# label says what has to happen before the ticket may be closed, and not every
# ticket needs one.
# THE GROUP IS THE PREFIX THE LABEL CARRIES. A row in group `area` is named
# `area:something`, and nothing else is accepted - lib/board.sh and lib/Board.psm1
# refuse the file otherwise. Without that rule a row filed under the wrong group is
# read by board-sync as the other family, and every ticket in the organisation is
# reported as missing a label that is right there on it.
# HOW THIS SET WAS DERIVED, on 2026-08-26: every issue of all eleven repositories of
# the organisation was read, open and closed, and every label application counted.
# 449 issues carried 814 label applications. 356 issues carry a `type:`, `area:` or
# `closes:` label; 24 carry one of the fourteen unprefixed families this file used to
# declare; 9 carry a GitHub default; 63 carry no label at all; exactly ONE issue
# carries both families. So the prefixed names below are not a new taxonomy - they
# are the one that was already in use, written down at last, and the fourteen names
# that were only ever created by labels-sync are gone.
# ONLY WHAT IS IN USE IS DECLARED. A label that exists in a repository but sits on no
# ticket is left out: labels-sync reports it under "not in labels.tsv, left alone"
# and nobody can put it on a new ticket until somebody adds the line. That is the
# intended way to grow this file - an area nobody has filed a ticket in would be a
# label that filters nothing. Eighteen such labels were measured and left out, and
# area:security came back the same day when alpha-cloud#124 took it, which is the
# growth this rule is for.
# ONE FILE FOR BOTH BOARDS. rules.md §8 requires one definition applied to every
# repository, because a label that exists in one repository and not another makes a
# board-wide filter lie. So an beta repository also carries the alpha areas
# and the other way round. Splitting the file per board would trade a filter that
# lies for a filter that cannot cross a board at all.
# COLOURS. Each type and each closes label has its own colour, because those are
# small closed sets and the colour is what you scan a column for. Every area label
# shares one colour, because that set is open and grows - they read as a family.
# area:install was retired in favour of area:installation. They named the same area
# in two repositories, so a filter on either missed the tickets that took the other.
type

column1: # WHAT WENT WRONG WITH THE TICKET, as opposed to what the ticket is about. An incident label
# says the ticket itself was written badly or filed when it should not have been. It is its own
# group, so it neither stands in for the type of work nor for the area it touches: an issue
# carrying one still needs its type and its area, and board-sync still reports it if it has
# neither. They share one colour because they read as one family, the way the areas do, and
# incident-count counts them per ISO week for exactly the question they exist to answer - how
# well the tickets themselves are written.
incident
